label: AMS demo boundary
query: Why is the Kyriba Source event safe to demo as full-spine while the AMS event is not?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings, the Kyriba Source event is demo-safe as a full-spine because its artifacts from Strategy through BAFO are actually built, stage-backed, and marked approved, whereas the AMS modernization event is only reliable through Evaluation and does not have completed, approval-backed downstream stages. Why Kyriba (LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026) has a “document-real” Source spine: Strategy, Sourcing, down through BAFO are present, aligned, and tagged as approved. That means every step of the Source lifecycle you’d show in a demo has real artifacts behind it, not stubs. For Kyriba, Executive Decision, Selection, Transition, and Value are explicitly still in review/needs-review, so you can demo them as “what comes next” but not as finalized outcomes. The key is that the upstream chain is coherent and governed. AMS (LSH-AMS-MODERNIZATION-2026) is only safe through Evaluation. Downstream stages (BAFO, Decision, Transition, Value) are either incomplete or not truth-backed, so portraying it as a full-spine decisioned program would misrepresent Lakeshore’s real state. Decision fork If you want a “this is what a complete Source journey looks like” demo: use Kyriba end-to-end and clearly label later stages as illustrative where they’re still needs-review. If you want to illustrate earlier-stage sourcing only: AMS is fine as a live example but should be constrained to Evaluation and prior.Evidence checked: intake.tenant_context (loaded tenant context), source_events.current_stage (sourcing stage and gate state), intake.question_scope (question scope), telemetry.answer_trace (answer trace).
